fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. God says, “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.” (Exodus 13:17) The road through the land of the Philistines was shorter, and He still steered them off it. It's like leaving your phone in the other room so you can't send that midnight text. God chose the road with that in view.

Yes, baker! “So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea.” (Exodus 13:18) Notice the word "around." It's the long way, and it's the way God picked. You know that moment when the GPS says "recalculating" and you're sure it's lost? Here the One choosing the route is God, and the text says He's the One leading.

Moab doesn't show up in these verses, baker. What the text gives is that God led the people “…around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea.” (Exodus 13:18) Wilderness, then the Red Sea. North isn't on this map at all, and I checked the corners twice.

True! “…the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.” (Exodus 13:18) Think about that. They're walking out of the house of slavery, and they're arrayed for battle. If it were me, I'd show up with a rolling pin and a big mustache. That's the verse's picture of them as they leave, and it's right in the same verse where God leads them the long way around.
